Phoenix Crossland is likely to miss the grand final. (Getty Images: Cameron Spencer)

Nathan Cleary has defended Phoenix Crossland against online abuse, saying the tackle that broke his leg was a "complete accident".

The Penrith star also said he had "nothing but respect" for Crossland, who had reached out to apologise.

Crossland has been referred straight to the judiciary over the tackle, with a hearing set for tonight at 6pm AEST.

Nathan Cleary has leapt to the defence of Newcastle hooker Phoenix Crossland, pleading with fans to stop peppering the embattled Knight with social media abuse as he prepares to plead his case to the NRL judiciary tonight.

Cleary confirmed on Monday night that Crossland had apologised for the hip-drop tackle that left him needing emergency surgery for a compound fracture and a dislocated ankle.

But less than 24 hours before Crossland was due to launch a desperate bid to play in the grand final, Cleary posted on Instagram from his hospital bed to offer support to the Knights number nine.

"Please don't be one of those people writing comments like this to Phoenix," Cleary posted alongside a graphic of some of the abuse Crossland had received.

Nathan Cleary says "I'll be back" in an upbeat Instagram post after successful surgery on his badly broken leg.

"It was a complete accident, and he doesn't deserve the unwarranted hate. He reached out to apologise, and I have nothing but respect for him.

"He's a competitor, and our game is made up of split-second moments that sometimes lead to unfortunate circumstances.

"Comments like this are so unfair. Spread love, not hate."

The comments against Crossland included accusations the tackle was deliberate and threats to maim the Knights dummy-half. Several are not suitable for print.

Crossland had almost appeared close to tears as Cleary was stretchered off Stadium Australia after the tackle and appeared to have accepted his fate even before referee Gerard Sutton sent him off.

He cut a dejected figure in the dressing room after being dismissed, before the Knights held on for a famous 22-14 win to qualify for the grand final.

Crossland seemed to accept his fate before it was even decided. (Supplied: Fox League)

Crossland was referred straight to the judiciary over the incident, with a hearing set for 6pm AEST tonight.

"We need to go down there and present a case to them, but it is a horrible accident at speed under fatigue," Knights director of football Chris James told ABC Sport.

"Phoenix Crossland has made more tackles in the NRL than any other player and he got one wrong.

"He got one wrong and it was a horrible injury for Nathan but that's not Phoenix's go. If you've ever met Phoenix Crossland, he's one of the great men of rugby league.

"Horrible for Nathan, the thoughts of our club go out to Nathan.

"He'll go down as one of the greats of the game and we hope he has a speedy recovery, but we'll also wrap our arms around Phoenix and make sure we look after him this week too."

The New Zealander will almost certainly be rubbed out of Sunday's grand final against the Sydney Roosters, with a question of how much of a ban extends to the World Cup.

The longest suspension handed down for a hip-drop tackle is five weeks. That would keep Crossland out of the World Cup final, if they qualify.
